body.x: Beatsomeone Corp. (CEO Yong-hwan Kim) participated in the 'Startup Zone' at the Eureka Park K-STARTUP integrated hall of 'CES 2023' in Las Vegas, USA from January 5 (Thursday) to 8 (Sunday, local time) for a total of 4 days.

Beatsomeone communicates with composers and fulfills all their music rights and management needs. Under the motto of “All music goes through Beatsomeone,” the company covers a broad content business area, from sound recording production, management, IP handling, publishing, and even album release, with a differentiator called Music+ICT.

In this exhibition, the startup introduced BY BEATS, a web-based cloud collaboration tool that protects composers' copyrights and keeps music files in an organized manner. The collaborative tool’s biggest benefit is that it is optimized for the music industry. A device is in place to prove the rights relationship among the people involved in the collaboration from the time music is produced. Another advantage is the ability to manage music files according to the digital version. These allow users to reuse the file at any time, even if the file is lost or deleted by mistake or error.

In addition, the mentoring function provides chances to ask questions and get answers from experts to boost users' work quality. Instead of delivering the files directly, the completed sound recordings can be streamed to a desired audience and sold in-service if desired. Also, users can safely and transparently manage their digital files and rights through blockchain NFT technology. A representative described that the service is well-received since it was developed after a series of interviews with many composers.

Beatsomeone was started based on CEO Yong-hwan Kim's experience from a well-known entertainer management enterprise for more than 15 years. He noticed that distributors manage some of the copyright after music is completed and released as albums, but no safeguards are in place during the actual music production. In addition, when multiple composers work on a single piece of music, the stake rates are verbally arranged and not honored. The agreements should be clear from the very beginning and honored. Not only that, collaborators often fail to properly version files, or they end up deleting files or stop their work altogether due to the lack of a system for music creation.

Currently, the number of music composers that Beatsomeone secured in South Korea is quickly growing, reaching 5,000 in 2021 and 17,000 in 2022. The firm won the Service Innovation Award in the sound recording production/sales platform area in October 2021, as well as the Best KNock IR Pitching Demo Day Award in November, successfully attracting Pre-Series A round investments in March 2022. Moreover, Beatsomeone was selected for a number of projects funded by the government to support technology development and commercialization.

As such, the music startup is moving toward the stage of synergy generation with global composers and artists, based on their initial achievements in South Korea. “Through this CES, we’d like to form partnerships and meet investors from larger music markets such as Southeast Asia, the United States and Europe,” explained a representative. “We look forward to connecting with overseas buyers looking for music contents, international businesses with singers/producers, and investors interested in music IPs or content.”

“Our plan is to target international composers, artists and corporate clients, securing over 50,000 members by 2023. Also, we are going to provide benefits to music students with plans geared toward them, as well as expand our expert mentor pool for junior composers and students.” As the companies goes forward, the representative explained that, "By collaborating with credible institutions that manage music rights in Korea, including the Korea Music Copyright Association, we are committed to ensuring rights for music creators and elevating the service to a profitable business.”

‘CES’ is the world’s biggest IT trade show and is a place where one can see the direction and trends of the appliance industry of the entire world. Hosted by the Consumer Technology Association (CTA), it is held annually in Las Vegas, USA in January. Having reported on CES for 17 consecutive years, AVING News started reporting news of CES to the entire world since 2006, and conducted ‘BEST OF CES’, which chose the most innovative product and technology, and ‘BEST OF MADE IN KOREA, which chose the best innovative company in Korea. In addition, it vividly relayed on-site issues in CES through ‘AVING LIVE’.

The K-STARTUP Joint Pavilion featured joint participation of institutions like the Korea Institute of Startup & Entrepreneurship Development, Seoul Business Agency, and Seoul Digital Foundation, as well as 51 Korean innovative companies, to enter the US market and discover global partners. In addition, university student supporters of CES 2023 chosen by each university (Kyunghee, Kookmin, Sogang, Chung-Ang) matched to participating companies based on their respective majors and fields of business.
